column1: # ============ THE CORRECTION: OLIVA WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THE INDEX ============
# On 14 September this archive recorded her as *** CAROLINA OLIVA ***, from the 1836 marriage
# petition - and said so twice, once correcting an earlier "not confidently legible" reading.
# FamilySearch's index of that petition also gives "Carolina Oliva", which is where the reading came
# from and what it was checked against.
# *** BOTH ARE WRONG. *** This 1837 act, in a different book and a different hand, writes
# CAROLINA ORIBE. The 1836 petition was then re-opened and magnified: the word carries a clear 'b'
# ascender and ends in 'e'. *** IT READS ORIBE THERE TOO. *** I followed the index and read what it
# had told me to expect.
# *** AND THE PUBLISHED GENEALOGY HAD IT RIGHT ALL ALONG. *** This archive's hypotheses page has
# carried, from a secondary tree, that Don Luis Lerena "married firstly a daughter of a ORIBE".
# That line has been sitting on the site the whole time, and it agrees with the registers.
# ---- WHAT THE NAME MEANS, STATED WITH CARE ----
# ORIBE is one of the great Uruguayan names. MANUEL ORIBE was President of the Republic 1835-1838
# and founder of the Blancos; his brother Ignacio was a general of the same wars. This family's
# other documented padrino is FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, Manuel Oribe's rival, president before him and
# founder of the Colorados - who stood at a Lerena font in 1831.
# *** NOTHING HERE SHOWS CAROLINA WAS KIN TO PRESIDENT ORIBE. *** Oribe is a surname, not a proof,
# and no record read so far names her parents. What IS on the record is that within five years this
# family had Rivera as a godparent and an Oribe as a bride - the two men whose quarrel became the
# Guerra Grande. That is recorded as a striking fact about their standing and connections, and as a
# question to pursue, NOT as a claim of descent from either house.
